bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the article's first page
bibliography.note: Lampert, W., Fleckner, W., Rai, H. & Taylor, B. E. 1986, L&O 31(3): 478–490, title as in the entry

claims.claim: Schöhsee grazing reached 170 % of the lake volume per day (Lampert et al. 1986; abstract only)
claims.source_value: 170 % per day of the UPPER 5 m's water (community grazing rate, a daily average of day and night profiles of the top 5 m, measured with ¹⁴C-labelled Scenedesmus), at the zooplankton peak in mid-May 1983 — not of the whole lake's volume
claims.location: p. 478 (PDF p. 1), abstract; p. 483 (PDF p. 6), Results; p. 484 (PDF p. 7), Fig. 8 caption
claims.quote: Grazing rates and biomasses are daily averages for the upper 5 m of water
claims.conditions: Schöhsee, Holstein (80 ha, max depth 30 m, mean 10.7 m, moderately eutrophic), sampled in a 13-m bay, spring 1983; the 170 %/d coincided with peak zooplankton biomass (nearly 80 % Daphnia, mainly D. galeata) and the greatest transparency (Secchi > 8 m in mid-May); grazing on the 1-µm Synechococcus was lower; the 'extremely high grazing' period was short
claims.note: the abstract's words are 'community grazing rates (170% of volume cleared per day)'; the body shows the volume is the upper 5 m. Write '170 % of the upper 5 m's water a day'. Now read in full, so 'abstract only' can go

claims.claim: a spring Daphnia peak can clear the water: 14–170 % of the lake filtered a day (Lampert et al. 1986; Luecke et al. 1990)
claims.source_value: Lampert gives the 170 %/d maximum, of the upper 5 m (as above); its lowest stated value is the 'typical summer' ~20 %/d reached by mid-June. The 14 % is not in Lampert et al.
claims.quote: By mid-June it had approached typical summer values of about 20%
claims.conditions: Schöhsee, spring 1983; daily averages for the upper 5 m, on Scenedesmus
claims.note: the 170 % needs the same 'upper 5 m' qualifier; the 14 % lower end must come from Luecke et al. 1990 (not checked here) and should be credited to it alone

notes: Context for §3.3.3: the Schöhsee clear-water phase came in MID-MAY (the paragraph's opening says 'late May or June' for the classic lakes); during it nearly 80 % of the zooplankton biomass was Daphnia, supporting 'the clear cases come from Daphnia-dominated lakes'; the algal decline was not tied to nutrient depletion or weather; night-time grazing in the top 5 m approached 10 % of the water an hour; small (< 35 µm) phytoplankton gave up to 88 % of primary production before the CWP, large particles more after; in enclosures without zooplankton, small particles always ended higher, while zooplankton stimulated large (> 35 µm) algae; during the CWP adult daphnids carried few or no eggs (food-limited). The paper also notes Lake Constance transparency rising from 1 to 10 m in a few days, and that a CWP is only apparent with weekly or more frequent sampling — relevant to why the eastern Maine medians show none.
